notes: Yama's 'Supplies' heading (Yama, revid 15292450): one 15/95.11 access roll grants a 'supply drop' that is three independent binary choices arriving together -- 'Either 3-4 pineapple pizzas or 3-4 wild pies', 'Either 2 prayer potion(3) or 2 super restore mix(2)', 'Either 1 super combat potion(1) or 1 Zamorak mix(2)' -- not six items competing for one slot. The raw wikitext carries six DropsLine rows at a uniform 7.5/95.11 each (half of the shared 15/95.11 access rate per pair, a clean 50/50 split within each choice), which the corpus-wide bundle detector (checkBundleSignals/findBundleGroups, build-tables.ts) cannot auto-confirm: its CO_DROP_PHRASES list matches 'dropped together'/'bundled with'-style footnotes, and this block's prose ('...chance of getting a supply drop. It will include: * Either A or B * Either C or D * Either E or F') is a different phrasing the detector does not recognise, and even if it did, its BundleGroup model only expresses one flat set of always-co-occurring items, not three separate nested pairs -- the same expressivity gap Mad Angel's compound shape hit. Modelled as three oneOf picks (each entry's own weight is the item's raw 7.5/95.11 share, `oneOf` needing only the RELATIVE 1:1 split within each pair) nested inside one always-mode table, spliced back into the main weighted pool as a single tableRef row at weight 15 -- matching Mad Angel's precedent exactly (data/overrides/mad-angel.json).
